debt_structure.eligibility_reason: Nimbus Textiles is a growing, profitable business but carries elevated leverage (3.81x Debt/EBITDA), near-ceiling WC utilisation (96.3%), four cheque bounces, thin liquidity (0.09 months cash cover), and material data-quality discrepancies that must be resolved before any new limit is sanctioned.

recommended_products.purpose: Unlock cash trapped in trade receivables to reduce CC/OD utilisation and ease day-to-day liquidity without adding EMI-bearing senior debt to an already stretched balance sheet
recommended_products.amount_basis: Eligible receivables (0-60 day) per dataroom ageing = INR 49,161,370. MIS ageing shows a higher total (INR 87,626,053) but the dataroom figure is used conservatively per data-quality flag 'mis_vs_dataroom_ageing'. Base advance rate 80% on 0-60d bucket = 0.80 × 49,161,370 = INR 39,329,096. Apply 25% concentration haircut on Vastra Global Exports LLP (40.3% of revenue; outstanding INR 35,092,141 per MIS): Vastra-attributable eligible receivables estimated at 40.3% × 49,161,370 = INR 19,802,032; haircut 50% of Vastra portion = reduce eligible base by 0.50 × 19,802,032 = INR 9,901,016; adjusted eligible base = 49,161,370 − 9,901,016 = INR 39,260,354; 80% advance = INR 31,408,283. Round down to INR 24,500,000 to stay within a conservative first-tranche limit given 4 cheque bounces and unresolved cash discrepancy; limit can step up to INR 31,000,000 upon resolution of data-quality flags.
recommended_products.repayment: self-liquidating — each invoice discounted is repaid directly from debtor collections within 30-90 day cycle; revolving within sanctioned limit
security: Assignment / hypothecation of specific invoices discounted
Escrow / collection account: all debtor payments routed through lender-controlled account
Personal guarantees of Mahesh Patel (55%) and Bhavna Patel (30%)
Negative lien on receivables not already charged to Bank of Baroda
covenants: Vastra Global Exports LLP concentration cap: single-debtor outstanding under this facility ≤ 35% of total discounted pool at any time
90+ day overdue receivables ≤ 15% of total trade receivables book (currently 20% per dataroom; step-down trigger)
Dilution rate (credit notes / disputes) ≤ 5% of discounted invoices per quarter
No additional borrowing without prior written consent
Monthly submission of updated debtor ageing within 7 days of month-end
Cheque bounce count ≤ 2 in any rolling 6-month window; breach triggers facility review

serviceability_check: Product is self-liquidating: repayment comes from debtor collections, NOT from Nimbus operating cash flows — no incremental DSCR burden on the borrower
Existing annual debt service (FY2025-26): interest INR 12,387,000 + TL principal (INR 820,000/month × 12) = INR 9,840,000; total = INR 22,227,000 (matches snapshot field 'annual_debt_service_inr')
Invoice discounting adds ZERO principal/interest EMI to debt service numerator — it is off-balance-sheet self-liquidating; DSCR unchanged at 1.33x post-facility

Discounting fee (9.75% p.a. on INR 24,500,000 for avg 60-day cycle) ≈ INR 24,500,000 × 9.75% × (60/365) = INR 393,493 per cycle — treated as a cost of funds, not a debt-service obligation; well within operating cash generation
Conclusion: DSCR post-facility = 1.33x ≥ 1.25x threshold; structure is serviceable

recommended_products.product: Cash Credit (CC/OD) — Restructuring / Rationalisation of Existing Facility
recommended_products.purpose: Restructure the existing Bank of Baroda Cash Credit (INR 70,000,000 sanctioned, INR 67,500,000 drawn, 96.4% utilised) by introducing a drawing-power discipline linked to a freshly reconciled stock + receivables statement, and adding a sub-limit carve-out for the invoice discounting facility to prevent double-financing of the same receivables
recommended_products.amount_basis: No increase in sanctioned limit recommended. Existing limit INR 70,000,000 retained. Drawing power to be recomputed monthly: 75% of eligible inventory (0-60d stock) + 75% of eligible receivables (0-60d, post-concentration haircut) net of creditors. At current inventory INR 50,076,000 and eligible receivables INR 39,260,354 (post-haircut, per invoice discounting sizing above): DP = 0.75 × 50,076,000 + 0.75 × 39,260,354 − 21,828,000 (trade payables) = 37,557,000 + 29,445,266 − 21,828,000 = INR 45,174,266. This implies the current outstanding of INR 67,500,000 exceeds recomputed DP by ~INR 22.3 million — a step-down plan is required (see covenants). Limit is not increased; restructuring only.
recommended_products.repayment: revolving — repaid from daily collections routed through CC account; annual renewal subject to satisfactory conduct
security: Existing first charge on current assets (inventory + receivables) — Bank of Baroda to confirm via updated charge registration
Personal guarantees of Mahesh Patel and Bhavna Patel (existing; to be reconfirmed)
Carve-out / sub-limit: receivables assigned to invoice discounting facility to be excluded from CC drawing-power computation to prevent double-financing
covenants: Drawing power recomputed monthly from stock + debtor statements submitted within 5 days of month-end; outstanding to be brought within DP within 30 days of each recomputation
Step-down plan: outstanding to reduce from INR 67,500,000 to ≤ INR 55,000,000 within 6 months and ≤ INR 45,000,000 within 12 months, consistent with invoice discounting releasing receivable cash
No double-financing: receivables discounted under the invoice discounting facility to be excluded from CC DP base
DSCR ≥ 1.25x on trailing 12-month basis, tested semi-annually
Current Ratio ≥ 1.15x tested semi-annually (current 1.13x — near-term cure required)
Cheque bounce count ≤ 2 in any rolling 6-month window; breach triggers immediate review and possible limit reduction
No additional secured borrowing without lender consent

serviceability_check: CC is a revolving facility — no fixed principal repayment; interest is the only recurring cost
Annual interest on CC at 10.6% on average outstanding ~INR 67,500,000 = INR 7,155,000

Step-down of CC outstanding by INR 22,500,000 over 12 months (funded by invoice discounting collections) will reduce interest cost by ~INR 2,385,000 p.a., improving DSCR to ~1.41x at steady state
Conclusion: DSCR post-restructuring ≥ 1.25x; structure is serviceable and improves over time

declined_products.product: New Term Loan (incremental capex or balance-sheet TL)
declined_products.reason: Debt/EBITDA already 3.81x (above 3.0x norm); DSCR headroom is thin at 1.33x; adding a new amortising TL with annual principal + interest would reduce DSCR below 1.25x. Example: a INR 20,000,000 TL at 11.5% over 48 months adds ~INR 5,000,000 annual principal + INR 2,300,000 interest = INR 7,300,000 incremental debt service; revised DSCR = 29,532,000 / (22,227,000 + 7,300,000) = 1.00x — below threshold.

declined_products.product: Incremental Working Capital Demand Loan (new WCDL beyond existing)
declined_products.reason: Existing WCDL (Tata Capital, INR 25,000,000) is 96% utilised; total WC limits are 96.3% drawn; adding a new WCDL increases leverage further above 3.81x Debt/EBITDA and adds bullet repayment risk given 4 cheque bounces and thin liquidity (0.09 months cash cover). Self-liquidating invoice discounting is the correct product to address the receivables-driven WC gap.

Weak governance flag (pledging status undisclosed), 4 cheque bounces, current ratio 1.13x below 1.2x covenant norm, and unresolved cash discrepancy of INR 35.9 million make an unsecured facility inappropriate at this time.

key_risks: Customer concentration (Vastra Global 40.3% of revenue, INR 35.1M outstanding): mitigated by 50% haircut on Vastra-attributable receivables in invoice discounting advance-rate computation and a 35% single-debtor cap covenant

Data-quality: INR 35.9M gap between balance-sheet cash and bank-statement closing, and INR 12.0M ageing discrepancy between MIS and dataroom — mitigated by using conservative (lower) figures for all sizing and making reconciliation a hard condition precedent before first drawdown
Thin DSCR headroom (1.33x): mitigated by recommending only self-liquidating invoice discounting (no new EMI burden) and a CC step-down plan that reduces interest cost over 12 months

Near-ceiling WC utilisation (96.3%) and 4 cheque bounces: mitigated by drawing-power discipline on CC, escrow routing of debtor collections, and a bounce-count covenant (≤2 per 6 months) with automatic review trigger
Elevated 90+ day receivables (20% per dataroom): mitigated by excluding 90+ day bucket from eligible base entirely and a covenant requiring 90+ days ≤ 15% of total book

Leverage above 3x norm (3.81x Debt/EBITDA): mitigated by declining all new senior debt, imposing a Debt/EBITDA step-down covenant to ≤3.5x within 12 months, and structuring the CC step-down to reduce absolute debt
rationale: Invoice discounting chosen as lead product because receivables (DSO 86-92 days) are the primary cash trap; self-liquidating structure adds zero EMI burden to a thin DSCR of 1.33x.
Eligible receivable base capped at INR 39.3M (post 50% Vastra haircut on 40.3% concentration) per concentration risk rules; first-tranche limit set conservatively at INR 24.5M.
No new senior amortising debt recommended: incremental TL of INR 20M would collapse DSCR to ~1.00x (29.5M EBITDA / 29.5M revised debt service) — below 1.25x threshold.
CC restructuring (not increase) addresses 96.4% utilisation; DP recomputation will require step-down from INR 67.5M to INR 45M over 12 months, reducing leverage toward 3.5x.
Data-quality flag 'bs_cash_vs_bank_statement' (INR 35.9M gap) is a hard CP: conservative balance-sheet cash of INR 2.6M used; bank-statement closing of INR 38.5M not credited until reconciled.
MIS vs dataroom ageing discrepancy (INR 11.99M) resolved conservatively by using lower dataroom figure (INR 75.6M total, INR 49.2M eligible 0-60d) for all advance-rate calculations.
Missing sanction letters for 2 of 3 facilities (flag 'sanction_letter_partial_coverage') are a CP: charge structure and pari-passu position cannot be confirmed without them.
Four cheque bounces in 12 months signal liquidity strain; bounce-count covenant (≤2 per 6 months) and escrow routing of collections are structural mitigants.
Promoter pledging status is undisclosed (null); disclosure and confirmation are a CP; personal guarantees from both promoters (85% combined holding) are required security.
Revenue growing at 8% YoY (FY24-26) and EBITDA margin stable at ~9.2% are positive; structure preserves headroom to step up invoice discounting limit to INR 31M once data flags are resolved.
Debt/EBITDA at 3.81x exceeds 3.0x norm; step-down covenant to ≤3.5x within 12 months and ≤3.0x within 24 months is embedded in CC restructuring terms.
Current ratio 1.13x is below 1.2x covenant norm; CC step-down and invoice discounting cash release are expected to improve it to ≥1.2x within two quarters — tested semi-annually.
